tex_content.html:
\begin{claim} \end{claim}[Volume noncollapsing from curvature bounded at the center] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0169, page-0170 ↗ prop:chow-iii-curvature-estimate-noncollapsed-balls 1. ch20:20.16\group Compactness

For curvature-normalized $n$-dimensional $\kappa $-solutions with Harnack, there is $c_0(\kappa ,n)>0$ such that \[ \Vol _{g_k(0)}B_{g_k(0)}(x_k,1)\ge c_0. \] \end{claim}
Proof

\sketch If the volumes tend to zero, choose $\delta _k\downarrow 0$ so that the volume ratio at radius $\delta _k$ is $\omega _n/2$ and rescale by $\delta _k^{-2}$. Proposition 2 gives curvature bounds on every fixed ball, hence a complete pointed limit. Its basepoint scalar curvature is zero, so the strong maximum principle makes it flat. Noncollapsing makes a complete flat limit Euclidean, contradicting the unit-ball volume $\omega _n/2$.
